author: David Schuman
title: Victim of Charlotte dog attack frustrated with city response, says she has PTSD - NewsBreak
text:
By David Schuman ,
2 hours ago
CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( QUEEN CITY NEWS ) — A Charlotte woman who was the victim of a vicious dog attack this year is angry over how city officials have responded to the incident.
PREVIOUS: Charlotte woman says her dogs ‘terrorized’ by neighbor’s German shepherds Pamela Bennett says she suffers from PTSD since the attack in March, when German shepherds leaped over her backyard fence in northeast Charlotte.
She says she was tackled and mauled, and her poodle, Walker, was nearly killed.
A neighbor heard the screams and ran to their rescue.
Bennett says Walker has fully recovered.
“My mental health is buoyed by how well he’s doing,” she said. “He has his sassiness back.”
Bennett installed a 6-foot chain-link fence to replace the lower, wooden one that the dogs hurdled.
Pamela Bennett. “I wasn’t safe in my own backyard,” she said.
Bennett says that with the new fence, her dogs are comfortable going in the yard again.
As for the dogs that attacked her, Bennett believes they belong to a man a couple of blocks away who received a containment order in January for unrestrained German shepherds.
Queen City News obtained videos from a complaint by another neighbor that contributed to that containment order.
Bennett is confident they’re the same dogs that attacked her.
Yet a Charlotte city spokesperson says the investigation remains open, and Animal Care and Control officers are still gathering information.
“I’m very frustrated because it’s not really resolved,” Bennett said. “I still have no accountability of the dog owner at all.”
Compounding Bennett’s frustration is the fact that ACC reports indicate the dogs were moved to the Fort Bragg area in May, more than two months after the attack.
Bennett feels the city’s delay in enforcing the containment order has destroyed the chance of any accountability for the owner.
“[Officers] have tools at their discretion, and I just want them to use them,” she said. “When they have a containment order, can they tie that to reports of other incidents with those same animals?”
Bennett says ACC officials admitted to her they “messed up.”
Bennett points out that the dogs could return to her neighborhood at any time.
“I’m scared,” she said. “I’m just really scared.”
A city spokesperson says ACC officers are now required to take photos of dogs in containment orders.
They weren’t doing that before this situation with Bennett began.
